name: Moidams – the Mound-Burial System of the Ahom Dynasty
description: In the forested foothills of the Patkai Ranges in eastern Assam, India, grassy domed mounds mark the royal burial ground of the Tai-Ahom dynasty. Over some 600 years, the Ahom buried kings and royals in hollow brick, stone or earth vaults, sometimes with horses, elephants and servants. Ninety moidams survive at the site, set among planted banyans and ponds, and Ahom ancestor rituals are still performed here.
